end.summary:
Practised rational-number examples briefly before coordinate geometry.
Reviewed quadrants, the origin, and ordered pairs.
Harsh attempted reading and plotting points from (x, y) pairs 9 times; 2 were unaided correct.
Harsh initially treated (3, 2) and (2, 3) as the same point; later stated that the first coordinate gives left-right and the second gives up-down, so the points differ.
Teach-back on the topic was not passed; the distinction was not confirmed after the last seen attempt.
end.parentNote: Asha practised ordered pairs, quadrants, the origin, and the rule “first x, then y.” Harsh explained that the first number shows left-right movement and the second shows up-down movement, which corrected the earlier mix-up between (3, 2) and (2, 3) during the lesson. At home, ask Harsh to plot pairs such as (3, 2) and (2, 3) on squared paper and label each movement separately.
